content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":5,"description_fidelity":5,"readability_1x":7,"pixel_craft":6,"palette_discipline":7,"appeal":6},"score":60,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["The silhouette reads more like a curled fish or seahorse than a floating squid; the lower blue mass forms one large hook instead of distinct gathered tentacles.","The oversized rectangular white eyes dominate the design and feel more like later fan-made pixel art than a compact Mega Man 2-3 enemy face.","The long black horizontal projection on the right reads as a stray bar or weapon rather than part of the creature.","Several outline areas are excessively heavy, especially around the eyes, center body, and lower-right curl, obscuring the internal forms at 1x.","The upper blue body has broad, plain color fields and a stepped diagonal contour without the economical mechanical panel details typical of Capcom enemies.","Four visible opaque colors are used closely together; the white, two blues, and black would require careful sprite layering to respect NES per-sprite palette limits.","Nothing in the static design clearly communicates its mine function or the red-eye warning state."],"fixes":["Replace the large lower curl with three short, separately readable tentacle tips, arranged in a compact gathered pose beneath the body.","Reduce each eye by roughly one pixel in width and height, round their outer corners, and separate them with a cleaner one-pixel black bridge.","Remove or shorten the right-side black bar so the outer contour ends immediately after the far eye.","Thin the heavy black regions around the center and lower-right edge to a consistent one-pixel outline wherever overlap is not required.","Reshape the top into a compact mechanical squid mantle with a more symmetrical dome and one small cyan highlight cluster.","Use black, one blue, and white as the primary sprite palette; reserve cyan or red for a layered highlight/eye-flash sprite.","Add a one- or two-pixel red eye state for the warning animation and create a second frame where the tentacles visibly spread backward for the thrust pulse."]}
